rules.title: Bump schema VERSION and upgrade_from range on every schema change
rules.problem: Reviewers repeatedly blocked Suggest PRs that changed CREATE TABLE statements (or the stored JSON shape) without bumping `pub const VERSION` in schema.rs and/or without moving the `upgrade_from` match range. Without the bump, existing on-device databases keep the old schema and queries fail or silently miss data.
rules.rule: If a PR changes any DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP TABLE|INDEX|TRIGGER, column list) in components/*/src/schema.rs or components/*/sql/*.sql, it must also change `VERSION` in the same crate, and `ConnectionInitializer::upgrade_from` must handle exactly versions < VERSION (for throw-away DBs like suggest: the last range end must be VERSION-1, never VERSION).
rules.detect: git diff origin/main -- 'components/*/src/schema.rs' 'components/*/sql/*.sql': if hunk text matches /\b(CREATE|ALTER|DROP)\s+(TABLE|INDEX|TRIGGER|VIEW)\b|^\s*[+-]\s*\w+\s+(INTEGER|TEXT|BLOB|REAL)\b/i and the line `pub const VERSION: u32 = N` is not in the diff -> fail. Second check (regex over schema.rs): parse `VERSION = N` and every range arm `a..=b` / `a..b` / literal in `fn upgrade_from`; fail if max handled version >= N or if (for migrating DBs like places/logins) no arm handles N-1.
rules.false_positive_risk: low — DDL changes inside comments or test-only schemas could trigger it; allow an explicit `// schema-version-unchanged: <reason>` marker.

rules.title: Foreign keys must declare ON DELETE behaviour
rules.problem: A detail table referenced suggestions(id) without ON DELETE CASCADE, so pruning suggestions would leave orphaned detail rows (unbounded growth / stale data). Later code in the chunk still adds REFERENCES without it.
rules.rule: Every `REFERENCES t(col)` clause in DDL must be followed by an explicit `ON DELETE CASCADE|SET NULL|RESTRICT`; and `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` must be set by the connection initializer of that DB.

rules.title: Use precise SQLite idioms (INSERT OR REPLACE, UNION ALL, typed DEFAULTs, NULL not sentinels)
rules.problem: Reviewers corrected MySQL-ism `REPLACE INTO`, `UNION` where `UNION ALL` was intended (needless dedup sort), `INTEGER ... DEFAULT ''` and `-1` sentinel columns used where NULL is meant.
rules.rule: In SQL strings: no bare `REPLACE INTO` (use `INSERT OR REPLACE`); `UNION` without `ALL` requires a `-- dedupe intended` comment; a column DEFAULT literal must match the declared affinity (INTEGER -> numeric, TEXT -> quoted); placeholder columns in UNION arms use `NULL AS col`, not -1/''.
rules.detect: regex on extracted SQL: /^\s*REPLACE\s+INTO/im; /\bUNION\b(?!\s+ALL)/i; /\b(INTEGER|INT|REAL)\b[^,]*DEFAULT\s+'/i; /SELECT[^;]*\b-1\s+AS\s+\w+/i.
rules.false_positive_risk: low — patterns are narrow; UNION dedupe can be whitelisted with a comment.

`''` is technically legal—SQLite's type system is [relaxed by default](https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html)—but let's use a number if the column is declared as a number.

Companion ast-grep: `$X.lock().unwrap()` -> remove unwrap after switching.

rules.title: Keep MutexGuard lifetimes explicit; never lock inside an if-let/match scrutinee
rules.problem: A remote_settings change did `if let Some(x) = self.remote_state.lock().field.clone() {...}` and then locked again inside the body — the temporary guard lives for the whole if-let, causing a deadlock; other threads used `drop(guard)` mid-function or re-acquired the lock leading to first-writer-wins races.
rules.rule: A `.lock()`/`.read()`/`.write()` call must not appear in the scrutinee of `if let`/`match`/`while let`; bind the needed value in its own statement or a `{ }` block. Avoid explicit `drop(guard)` in favour of a scope block, and document assumptions when a lock is released and re-acquired.

rules.false_positive_risk: medium — nursery lints have some FPs; scope to component crates.
